gaps.location: pi_b72f1812c354b429a79086f8, proof paragraph beginning “The property is local at o”
gaps.issue: After sheafification, each term v_n of a decreasing sequence is only known to satisfy the mixed inequality on some neighborhood U_n of o. These neighborhoods may shrink, so no fixed atom configuration is necessarily covered for every n. Passing to the limit in a finite weighted sum requires inequalities on a common chart, which the proof does not establish. The observation that one cover member contains o proves locality but does not resolve this uniformity problem. Consequently, the transfinite induction and the resulting exclusion from the full generated sheaf are not justified.

repair_hints: [pi_b72f1812c354b429a79086f8] Carry branchwise convexity as a simultaneous invariant through the construction. Use it to propagate the mixed inequality from a smaller neighborhood to any fixed product chart: scale admissible atoms to t z_a and apply v(t z_a) ≤ (1−t)v(o)+t v(z_a), together with the small-neighborhood inequality. Handle v(o)=−∞ separately. Then justify decreasing limits and sheafification using this strengthened invariant.
